The maker's own summary in plugin.json calls this a dual sequencer and clock divider, which is the 4Seq text repeated; the panel subtitle, Random Voltage Source, matches what the code does.

lines: A chaotic oscillator with no inputs at all, giving two slowly wandering voltages from a modelled analogue circuit that never repeats
Adds up to 10 kilohms to a fixed 100 kilohms in the modelled circuit, which changes how long the voltages spend around one of the two attractors rather than the other; it does not change the rate
The wider-swinging of the two voltages, the one the lamp follows: green while it is positive, red while it is negative, full brightness at 2V
The narrower-swinging of the two voltages, taken from a different node of the same circuit
Note — there is nothing to patch in and no clock to give it: the circuit runs from the moment the module is added and both outputs are moving straight away.
Note — one turn around the pair of attractors takes roughly 15 to 30 seconds, so a change at the knob takes minutes rather than seconds to show itself.
SlothTorpor.notes: The circuit is Don Cross's model of the hardware, solved by iteration each sample (SlothCircuit.hpp:124-196). The knob is the variable part of one resistance, 100k in series with 0 to 10k (SlothCircuit.hpp:100). The orbit times are the maker's README rather than anything in the code; the code differs between the three modules only in a time dilation factor and a starting capacitor voltage (SlothCircuit.hpp:200-224). No voltage range is stated anywhere for the two outputs, so none is given here.

lines: A three-input mixer feeding a four-stage shift register, with two feedback paths from the last stage back into the mixer
Scales OUT 4 into a modelled diode before that feedback reaches the mixer, 0 to 4; the diode squares its input, so the effect grows far faster than the knob turns
Scales whatever arrives at IN 3 into the mixer, passing nothing fully anticlockwise and full level fully clockwise; with IN 3 empty it scales OUT 4 back into the mixer instead

The mixer's total clamped to -10V to 10V, taken afresh on every fourth clock and held between times
The value OUT 1 took, copied here one clock later
The value OUT 1 took, copied here two clocks later
The value OUT 1 took, copied here three clocks later, and the one both feedback controls read
Note — nothing moves without a clock: patch one into CLOCK and the four outputs fill in turn, OUT 1 taking a new mixer value on every fourth clock.
Note — both feedback knobs come up fully anticlockwise, so with nothing patched all four outputs stay at 0V however fast the clock runs.
Note — the linear feedback path is the IN 3 knob and it is only there while IN 3 is empty; the nonlinear path through the diode is always in circuit and is subtracted rather than added.
SquidAxon.notes: OUT 1 is the mixer, not a register stage: it is written only when the internal stage counter is at zero, which is every fourth clock (SquidAxon.cpp:72-93), and the maker's README makes the same point. The nonlinear feedback is OUT 4 times the knob, through a squared diode model, clamped to -9V to 9V and then multiplied by -0.7 before being added to the mix (SquidAxon.cpp:85-90). The three inputs are only read at a clock, so anything patched into them is sampled rather than followed.

Adds up to 10 kilohms to a fixed 100 kilohms in that circuit, which changes how long it spends around one of its two attractors rather than the other; it does not change the rate

The narrower-swinging of that circuit's two chaotic voltages

That circuit's Y voltage inverted, with a fifth of its CV input added
The inertia circuit's Y voltage inverted; inertia has no CV input, so nothing is added to it
The three Z voltages combined while that total is negative, down to the circuit's own limit, and 0V at any other time; the total is 0.7 times torpor's Z less apathy's Z and inertia's Z added together

Note — there is nothing to patch in to make this work: all three circuits run from the moment the module is added and every output is moving straight away.
Note — inertia has neither a knob nor a CV input; one turn around its attractors takes roughly 30 to 40 minutes, against 60 to 90 seconds for apathy and 15 to 30 seconds for torpor.
Note — the Z outputs here are the inverted form of the Y output the single Sloth modules give, which is why the panel has three outputs per circuit where they have two.
TripleSloth.notes: Z is the circuit's z node, which SlothCircuit.hpp:159 computes as minus the Y voltage minus the CV scaled by 100k over 470k, about a fifth; with no CV patched Z is simply Y inverted. The combined output pair splits the value at TripleSloth.cpp:125-127, which is the formula in the maker's README. The CV inputs take a polyphonic cable and sum its channels to one, and the maker does not tag the module polyphonic.
